content: Increased bowel sounds, also referred to as hyperactive bowel sounds, can sometimes be audible even without the use of a stethoscope. Hyperactive bowel sounds indicate an increase in intestinal activity, which may occur in association with diarrhea or following food consumption. In some cases, very high-pitched bowel sounds may suggest the presence of an early bowel obstruction. The majority of sounds originating from the stomach and intestines are related to normal digestive processes and are typically not a cause for concern. However, various conditions can lead to either hyperactive or hypoactive bowel sounds. Most of these conditions are benign and do not require medical treatment. A thorough patient history is essential for evaluating the underlying cause of increased bowel sounds. Flat and upright X-rays are valuable tools for assessing the potential causes of these sounds. Additionally, abdominal CT scans are highly effective in identifying the etiology. Enteroclysis, a specialized diagnostic study, can be used to evaluate the degree of bowel obstruction. In cases of complete bowel obstruction, surgical intervention is generally required to resolve the condition.
